claim: Sobrino de Botin in Madrid is the Guinness-confirmed oldest restaurant in the world, opened 1725, and kept its 300-year-old oven lit even during the COVID lockdown.
quote: Opened in 1725 in the center of Madrid, it's the longest continuously running restaurant on record... they even stoked the flames of their 300-year-old oven every day during the Covid-19 pandemic

claim: Botin's official site confirms it is the world's oldest restaurant founded 1725, specializing in roast suckling pig (cochinillo) and roast lamb at Calle Cuchilleros 17, Madrid.
quote: Botin Restaurant. The oldest restaurant in the world. 300th Anniversary | Roast Suckling Pigs and Lamb of Madrid

claim: Botin's signature cochinillo asado appears in the closing pages of Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises, and the restaurant was opened by Frenchman Jean Botin in 1725.
quote: the restaurant and its speciality of cochinillo asado (roast suckling pig) are mentioned in the closing pages of Ernest Hemingway's novel The Sun Also Rises

claim: Els Quatre Gats opened June 12, 1897, founded by Pere Romeu, Santiago Rusinol, Ramon Casas and Miquel Utrillo; a 17-year-old Picasso became a regular and held his first solo exhibition there in 1899, designing its letterhead.
quote: A young 17-year-old Pablo Picasso... became a regular patron. In 1899, he made his first individual exhibition of paintings at 4Gats and designed the restaurant's letterhead.

claim: Els Quatre Gats was conceived as a place for 'food of the spirit' where modernist artists including Gaudi gathered; it closed in 1903 and was revived in 1978.
quote: the four men who founded it wanted the cafe to be known... for having 'food of the spirit'... a popular haunt for important modernist and bohemian artists of the day, including architects such as Antoni Gaudi

claim: Petritegi cider house near San Sebastian traces its press farmhouse to 1526, with six generations of the Otano-Goikoetxea family making cider since 1890, serving txotx-style straight from the barrel.
quote: The origin of the Petritegi cider maker dates back to 1526... Since 1890, six generations of the Otano-Goikoetxea family have kept the cider-making tradition alive.

claim: Basque sagardotegi cider houses descend from an 11th-century tradition; before the Civil War the area had ~800 sidrerias, now barely 100 survive, with the txotx ritual central to the experience.
quote: Before the Spanish Civil War there were around 800 sidrerias in the area; now barely a hundred keep the tradition alive.

claim: Martinho da Arcada (est. 1782) is Lisbon's oldest restaurant, sits under the arcades of Praca do Comercio, and keeps a table permanently reserved for poet Fernando Pessoa who frequented it until days before his 1935 death.
quote: Established in 1782, Martinho da Arcada... still has a table permanently reserved for long-dead poet Fernando Pessoa.

claim: Cafe Martinho da Arcada, established 1782, is recognized on the Historic Cafes Route as a literary meeting point and Pessoa's haunt serving classic Portuguese cuisine.

A Ginjinha (Ginjinha Espinheira), opened 1840 just off Rossio square, was Lisbon's first bar to sell ginjinha cherry liqueur, run by the same family for five generations and designated a Loja Com Historia.
quote: The A Ginjinha bar originally opened in 1840, and has been run by the same family for five generations... This was the first bar to sell ginjinha in Lisbon, and is a designated Loja Com Historia
